subject: science
title: Be a Scientist
about: How a scientist works: observing with the five senses, the tools (hand lens, ruler, thermometer, balance scale, timer) and what each one shows, asking a question, trying it, writing down what you see, and staying safe with goggles and no tasting. Science practices are not a standard of their own in NC's 2023 Grade 1 science; this bridge deck sits under PS.1.1.2, the objective that has children carry out investigations, compare and collect data.
tip: Hand him a hand lens and a ruler and let him be the scientist for one leaf: look, measure, say what he sees, then draw it.

cards.q: Which part of your body do you use to see the color of a rock?
cards.note: Looking closely at something is called observing.

cards.q: You hear a bird sing. Which sense are you using?
cards.note: Your ears are for hearing. Close your eyes and you can still observe with your ears.

cards.q: You sniff a flower. Which sense is that?
cards.note: Your nose is for smell. Smell can tell you a banana is ripe.

cards.q: You feel a rock and it is rough. Which sense tells you that?
cards.note: Your skin is for touch. Rough, smooth, warm and cold are things you feel.

cards.q: An apple is sweet. Which sense tells you that?
cards.note: Your tongue is for taste. In science, only taste food a grown-up says is safe.

cards.q: How many senses do you have?
cards.note: Sight, hearing, smell, touch and taste. One for each finger.

cards.q: What tool makes a tiny bug look bigger?
cards.note: A hand lens is a magnifying glass. It helps your eyes see small things.

cards.q: What tool do you use to measure how long a leaf is?
cards.note: A ruler measures length in inches or centimeters.

cards.q: What tool tells you how hot or cold the water is?
cards.note: Say ther-MOM-uh-ter. It measures temperature, how hot or cold something is.

cards.q: What tool tells you which rock is heavier?
cards.note: Put one rock on each side. The heavier side goes down.

cards.q: You want to know how long a toy car keeps rolling. What tool do you use?
cards.note: A timer measures time. Start it when the car starts and stop it when the car stops.

cards.q: A scientist wonders why the ice melted. What does the scientist do first?
cards.note: Science starts with a question, like why did the ice melt?

cards.q: You wonder if a toy boat floats. How do you find out?
cards.note: Scientists try things to find out. Trying it is called an investigation.

cards.q: You see the bean plant grow taller. What do you do so you remember?
cards.note: Scientists write or draw what they see. That is called recording.

cards.q: What do we call looking very closely at something?
cards.note: Say ob-ZER-ving. You can observe with all five senses, not just your eyes.

cards.q: What do you wear to keep your eyes safe in science?
cards.note: Goggles keep splashes and bits out of your eyes.

cards.q: You find a jar of strange powder in science class. What do you do?
cards.note: Never taste or eat something in science unless a grown-up says it is safe.

cards.q: You finish a science experiment with soil. What do you do with your hands?
cards.note: Clean hands after science keep germs and dirt off your snack.
